stage_1_predict.prompt: Before calculating numerical values: If a sum of money amounts to A_2 after 2 years and A_3 after 3 years under annual compound interest, how do you determine whether the annual interest rate is higher than 15% without knowing the original principal P?
options: A. You cannot determine it because P is an unknown free parameter.
B. Evaluate the ratio A_3 / A_2: if A_3 / A_2 > 1.15, the rate r exceeds 15% because A_3 / A_2 = 1 + r/100.
C. Subtract A_2 from A_3 and divide by 2.
D. Take the square root of A_3 / A_2.
stage_1_predict.predict_rationale: Forces the learner to recognize that in geometric compounding, the quotient of adjacent terms isolates the common ratio 1 + r/100, completely independent of the initial scale factor P.

stage_2_attempt.task: A cistern has two fill pipes P and Q which can fill it in 12 hours and 16 hours respectively. A waste pipe R empties the full cistern in 24 hours. Formulate the exact net hourly rate equation and determine the time required to fill the cistern when all three pipes are opened simultaneously.

model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.step_1: Hourly fill rates: R_P = 1/12, R_Q = 1/16; hourly empty rate: R_R = 1/24.
model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.step_2: Net rate equation: R_{net} = 1/12 + 1/16 - 1/24. Common denominator of (12, 16, 24) is 48.
model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.step_4: Total time to fill = 1 / R_{net} = 48 / 5 hours = 9.6 hours (or 9 hours 36 minutes).
model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.conclusion: The cistern will fill in 9 hours 36 minutes.

dialog_steps.inquiry: Suppose you measure that a tank took 8 hours to fill with an unnoticed leak, but its nominal fill time without the leak was 6 hours 40 minutes (20/3 hours). Working BACKWARDS from the observed delay, how do you isolate the leak's standalone emptying time?
dialog_steps.expected_insight: Convert the observed actual duration to net rate R_{actual} = 1/8. Convert nominal duration to nominal rate R_{nominal} = 3/20. The difference between nominal and actual rates is precisely the leak rate: R_{leak} = R_{nominal} - R_{actual} = 3/20 - 1/8 = 1/40. Thus the leak alone empties the tank in 40 hours!

dialog_steps.inquiry: Why must you subtract rates rather than subtracting the delay of 1 hour 20 minutes from the 6h 40m?
dialog_steps.expected_insight: Because time does not flow in a linear pool; during those extra 80 minutes, the inlet pipes were STILL pouring water in while the leak was leaking! Only rates quantify the instantaneous volumetric balance.

stage_4_boundary_test.prompt: Perturbation & Boundary Test: Suppose the leak rate R_{leak} is continuously increased until it equals the combined inlet rate R_{in} (R_{leak} = R_{in}). What happens to the fill time T, and what happens if R_{leak} > R_{in}?
options: A. If R_{leak} = R_{in}, T = 0; if R_{leak} > R_{in}, the tank fills instantly.
B. If R_{leak} = R_{in}, net rate is 0 and T -> infinity (tank never fills); if R_{leak} > R_{in}, net rate is negative and water level continuously falls.
C. The tank pressure explodes due to equilibrium.
D. Filling time becomes negative, which means it filled in the past.
stage_4_boundary_test.explanation: At R_{leak} = R_{in}, R_{net} = 0, so T = 1/0 -> infinity. For R_{leak} > R_{in}, net outflow exceeds inflow, proving that positive steady-state filling is only physically possible when R_{in} > R_{leak}.

hint_1_conceptual_nudge.text: Never add or subtract times directly in work/rate problems. Convert every action into fractional capacity per unit time (rates), combine rates linearly, and take the reciprocal of the net rate to find the total time.

hint_2_tactical_step.text: For compound interest, write down A_2 = P(1 + r/100)^2 and A_3 = P(1 + r/100)^3. Form the quotient A_3 / A_2 to eliminate P immediately.
